title: Ice Chamber Experiment Metagenome
description: Eukaryotic and bacterial populations have been observed on young sea ice and in frost flowers, however, local geography and ocean and air currents can interfere with determining the local driving forces controlling microbial distribution on sea ice. Here, we report the use of the Roland von Glasow Air-Sea-Ice Chamber, a large laboratory-scale sea ice chamber, to reduce global environmental effects on the driving forces for microbial colonization of frost flowers. The taxonomic and functional partitioning of bacteria into distinct niches (frost flower, brine, ice matrix and seawater) consistent with niche-based selection was bolstered by the appearance of archetypal sea ice bacteria, not identified in the seeding seawater. In contrast, the consistency of eukaryotic communities across the profile reflected stochasticity. Bacterial enrichment in sea ice occurred at a similar rate as previously observed, despite minimal diatom representation.
